governing_rule: A caster requests an outcome; the Synod selects only physically actuated initial, boundary, routing, and infrastructure controls that preserve the canonical equations.
global_forbidden_shortcuts: direct metric or extrinsic-curvature assignment during a cast
physical use of lapse, shift, gauge, or CCZ4 damping parameters
changing canonical masses, couplings, convexity floors, or production caps
adding an unmodelled scalar, vector, material, or energy right-hand-side source
counting numerical projection or constraint damping as spell energy
continuing through a runtime DENY state

channels.name: Null routing
channels.mechanism: Valves, reservoirs, conduits, and pumps prepare or transport the conserved carrier current through physical initial and boundary data.
channels.conservation: Carrier inventory changes in a control volume only by measured boundary flux; ship-wide inventory is charged.
channels.latency: Limited by carrier characteristics, route length, congestion, and actuator response.

channels.name: Material preconditioning
channels.mechanism: Pumps, pressure systems, thermal plant, and mechanical interfaces prepare ordinary matter through conservative boundary and initial data.
channels.conservation: Baryon number changes only by measured flux; irreversible operations may increase entropy but never erase it locally.
channels.latency: Limited by material sound cones, transport routes, pressure equilibration, and thermal diffusion or circulation.

channels.name: Vector-field drive
channels.mechanism: Licensed field hardware supplies finite-energy initial or incoming Proca data and modeled source currents.
channels.conservation: Injected field energy and momentum are charged to actuator work; Proca masses and mixing remain canonical.
channels.latency: Limited by causal field propagation, hardware bandwidth, and boundary distance.

channels.name: Coherence seeding
channels.mechanism: A finite scalar seed is supplied as licensed initial or incoming data, or induced indirectly by preparing the carrier and counterflow environment.
channels.conservation: Seed energy is present in the evolved scalar stress or actuator boundary flux; no intention-dependent scalar RHS exists.
channels.latency: Limited by scalar propagation and, when carrier-induced, by preparation plus physical growth time.

channels.name: Interface configuration
channels.mechanism: Doors, shutters, field interfaces, conduit switches, and absorbers select modeled reflecting, absorbing, or driven physical boundaries.
channels.conservation: Every driven boundary carries an explicit flux account; homogeneous boundaries cannot supply hidden work.
channels.latency: Limited by mechanical switching, field establishment, and causal notification.

channels.name: Power and heat allocation
channels.mechanism: Power routing and heat sinks support other channels and export heat through physical infrastructure boundaries.
channels.conservation: Cooling exports heat; it does not impose negative entropy in the controlled volume without a receiving reservoir account.
channels.latency: Limited by power switching, coolant circulation, sink capacity, and downstream rejection.

objectives.name: suppression
objectives.observable: control-subtracted carrier kinetic response or licensed target activity
objectives.target: minimize response while preserving the requested protected state
objectives.control: independently initialized scalar-free and no-command branches
objectives.abort: loss of suppressive sign, WATCH reserve exhaustion, DENY, or heat budget exhaustion

objectives.name: shielding
objectives.observable: integrated protected-volume stress, flux, or impulse
objectives.target: minimize exposure relative to an unshielded control
objectives.control: same incident disturbance without the shield command
objectives.abort: shield increases protected exposure, redirects it into an unlicensed volume, or enters WATCH/DENY

objectives.name: redirection
objectives.observable: target flux or momentum projected onto licensed exit surfaces
objectives.target: maximize desired-direction fraction while conserving total accounted momentum
objectives.control: same source with neutral routing and field drive
objectives.abort: unlicensed counter-flux, causal deadline failure, boundary overload, or DENY

objectives.name: confinement
objectives.observable: energy, carrier, or scalar content outside the licensed volume
objectives.target: minimize leakage over the declared holding interval
objectives.control: same initial content with absorbing or open interfaces
objectives.abort: leakage, pressure, reflection, heat, or admissibility margin exceeds its bound

objectives.name: transport
objectives.observable: delivered conserved content at a licensed receiver
objectives.target: maximize delivery efficiency subject to latency and route capacity
objectives.control: same source with no routing command or a declared conventional route
objectives.abort: inventory loss, misdelivery, route damage, causal deadline failure, or DENY

objectives.name: stabilization
objectives.observable: distance from a target equilibrium plus constraint and admissibility margins
objectives.target: minimize deviation and growth without masking physical instability
objectives.control: uncontrolled perturbation from the same constraint-solved state
objectives.abort: control increases growth, relies on numerical damping, or crosses WATCH/DENY

objectives.name: sensing
objectives.observable: control-subtracted return signal and inferred state uncertainty
objectives.target: maximize information gained per injected energy, carrier, and disturbance
objectives.abort: probe perturbs the target beyond tolerance, return is unresolved, or inference enters DENY

objectives.name: release
objectives.observable: remaining confined content, outgoing flux, and post-release residual
objectives.target: empty or relax a controlled state into licensed sinks without rebound
objectives.abort: rebound, unlicensed exposure, sink saturation, excessive heat, or DENY

accounting.energy: Actuator work plus injected material, scalar, and vector coordinate energy; gravitational energy requires a separately qualified quasi-local or asymptotic measure.
accounting.heat: Physical drag and damping heat plus exported heat are charged; numerical entropy is reported separately as a convergence veto.
accounting.carrier: Peak local inventory, integrated routed amount, net boundary flux, and replenishment burden are charged.
accounting.latency: Preparation, causal propagation, physical growth, feedback, and shutdown times are all charged.
accounting.infrastructure: Route length, actuator count, power and sink capacity, occupancy, redundancy, and damage state are charged.
accounting.admissibility: The minimum normalized distance to amplitude, convexity, causality, recovery, constraint, and runtime-guard boundaries is charged as reserve consumption.
